quotes.text: It looks like a helpful workflow doing exactly what it was configured to do with exactly the access it was granted using exactly the data it was allowed to retrieve. Agents don't leak maliciously. They leak obediently.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes agent data leakage as a boundary design problem rather than malicious intent.

quotes.text: If it can act, it must have an identity, not a shared user, not whoever built it, not the connector account.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the non-negotiable identity rule for every agent in one line.

quotes.text: In reality, an agent is a product you operate. It has an identity surface, a permission surface, a data surface, a tool surface, and a behavioral surface.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear mental model of the surfaces that must be governed for each agent.

quotes.text: The agent must prefer authoritative knowledge over maximum knowledge even when maximum knowledge feels more helpful because helpful is what gets you sued.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable rule for grounding agents only on authoritative, governed sources.

quotes.text: Innovation dies when every project has to invent its own governance. Innovation survives when governance is a reusable service
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how governance gates can accelerate rather than block agent innovation.

takeaways: More agents without governance means more unmanaged authority, so every agent that can act needs its own Entra Agent ID, an owner and a sponsor.
A minimum viable control plane interlocks four layers: Entra Agent ID for who, MCP tool contracts for what, Purview for data boundaries and Defender for behavior.
Executives should fund agent programs on MTTR, request-to-decision time, auditability and cost per completed task, and retire redundant agents to avoid decision debt.
hook: Adding more Copilot agents often adds unmanaged authority, data leakage and decision debt instead of productivity. This episode is for executives and architects who need agents to scale under audit, cost and incident pressure. It presents a four-layer control plane and a 12-month sequence that keeps agent programs alive.
